instruction: Export both open blog pages to PDF format and place them in the /home/user/Documents/Blog folder.

metadata.explanation: This variation checks if exactly 2 PDF files are created in the /home/user/Documents/Blog folder, verifying that both blog pages were exported to PDF format.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly counts PDF files in the target folder using appropriate bash command
Metric comparison logic is correct: checks if count equals expected value (2)
Expected count (2) matches instruction requirement (both blog pages)
Postconfig ensures target directory exists before verification
Getter handles edge case where no PDFs exist (2>/dev/null)
LIMITATION: Evaluator only verifies COUNT of PDFs, not their CONTENT or SOURCE
Cannot verify if the 2 PDFs are actually exports of the specified blog pages vs any random PDFs
For practical purposes, count-based verification is reasonable given PDF content verification complexity
Assumes folder is initially empty (acceptable due to postconfig creating fresh directory)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding filename pattern verification (e.g., PDFs should contain keywords from blog URLs or titles)
Consider checking PDF file sizes to ensure they are substantial (not empty or corrupted)
Consider verifying PDF creation timestamps to ensure they were created during task execution
Could enhance by checking PDF metadata (e.g., page count > 0, or title metadata matching blog titles)
